questions.q: A server is no longer in the inventory and no tool monitors it. Which term applies?
questions.explain: Unmanaged means outside management and inventory. Unsupported means the vendor no longer provides support.

questions.q: A file is verified as safe and then replaced before it is opened. Which vulnerability is this?
questions.explain: The gap between time-of-check and time-of-use is exploited: this is a race condition.

questions.q: Which attack surfaces relate to identity or configuration? (Select all that apply)
questions.explain: All four are attack surfaces: forgotten credentials, unauthorized devices, unapproved services, and misconfigured public storage.

questions.q: Match each scenario to its vulnerability category.

pairs.left: API key in a public repository
Flaw with no known vendor patch
User logged into an unapproved service
Wireless network with a rogue access point

questions.explain: The category depends on the nature of the weakness, not the attacker's tool.

questions.q: Which control is most appropriate when facing a zero-day?
options: Reduce the attack surface, segment, and detect anomalous behavior
Add the CVE to an exclusion list
questions.explain: Without a patch or known signature, attack surface reduction, segmentation, and behavioral detection remain effective.

questions.q: Which concept is absent from the four textbooks but required in objective 2.4?
options: Large language models (LLMs) as an attack surface
questions.explain: LLMs, IdPs, public repositories, and public object storage are gaps in the textbooks: covered in the official exam objectives only.
